claims.statement: Mo has a history as a name for the panda and as a composite creature depicted in Chinese tradition.
claims.statement_id: Mo memiliki sejarah sebagai nama panda sekaligus penggambaran makhluk campuran dalam tradisi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: Mo (Chinese: 貘) was the Chinese name for the giant panda from the 3rd century BCE to the 19th century CE. ... Chinese woodblocks depict the mò (貘) as having an elephant trunk, rhinoceros eyes, cow tail and tiger paws, following the description of 9th-century Tang poet Bai/Bo Juyi.

claims.statement: Bai Juyi describes Mo with an elephant trunk, rhinoceros eyes, a cow tail, and tiger paws.
claims.statement_id: Dalam uraian Bai Juyi, Mo menggabungkan belalai gajah, mata badak, ekor sapi, dan kaki harimau.
claims.quote: The mò has elephant trunk, rhinoceros eyes, cow tail, and tiger paws [貘者象鼻犀目牛尾虎足]. It inhabits the mountains and valleys of the south. To sleep on its pelt repels contagion [寢其皮辟瘟]. To draw its form repels evil [圖其形辟邪]. In the past I suffered from wind-ailment of the head [病頭風], and whenever I slept I always protected my head with a small screen.

claims.statement: Bai Juyi associates images of Mo with warding off evil and its pelt with protection from contagion.
claims.statement_id: Bai Juyi mengaitkan gambar Mo dengan penolakan pengaruh jahat dan kulitnya dengan perlindungan dari wabah.
claims.quote: The mò has elephant trunk, rhinoceros eyes, cow tail, and tiger paws [貘者象鼻犀目牛尾虎足]. It inhabits the mountains and valleys of the south. To sleep on its pelt repels contagion [寢其皮辟瘟]. To draw its form repels evil [圖其形辟邪]. In the past I suffered from wind-ailment of the head [病頭風], and whenever I slept I always protected my head with a small screen.

claims.statement: The Japanese baku develops the protective image motif into dream devouring to prevent nightmares.
claims.statement_id: Baku Jepang mengembangkan motif gambar pelindung kesehatan menjadi makhluk pemakan mimpi buruk.
claims.quote: The Japanese baku (獏) changed the Chinese myth about the mò image preventing illness to dream-devouring in order to prevent nightmares.

claims.statement: The metal eating description comes from Guo Pu's commentary rather than the early Shan Hai Jing text itself.
claims.statement_id: Uraian pemakan logam berasal dari komentar Guo Pu, bukan langsung dari teks awal Shan Hai Jing.
claims.quote: Bai's "eats iron and copper, and eats nothing else" reference comes from Guo Pu's 4th century commentary to the Shanhai jing and not the pre-Han classic text. The Shanhai jing proper mentions the mengbao "ferocious leopard" on South Mountain, which Guo notes as a metal-eating beast similar to the mò, and mentions Lai Mountain, which he glosses as a mò habitat.

claims.statement: Until the late Qing, Mo could refer to both the panda and the composite creature, before a mistaken identification associated it with the tapir.
claims.statement_id: Hingga akhir Qing, nama Mo masih mencakup panda dan makhluk campuran, sebelum dikaitkan dengan tapir melalui kekeliruan identifikasi.
claims.quote: Up until the late Qing dynasty (1644–1912), the Chinese name mo (貘) continued referring to both "giant panda" and "chimera with an elephant trunk, rhinoceros eyes, cow tail, and tiger paws", and owing to Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat's mix-up in the 1820s, mò was misidentified as the recently discovered "Malayan tapir".

claims.statement: In Bai Juyi's preface the mo has an elephant's nose, rhinoceros eyes, an ox tail and tiger feet, and lives in the mountain valleys of the south; sleeping on its skin averts pestilence and drawing its form averts evil.
claims.statement_id: Dalam pengantar Bai Juyi, Mo digambarkan berbelalai gajah, bermata badak, berekor sapi, dan berkaki harimau, hidup di lembah-lembah pegunungan di selatan; tidur di atas kulitnya menolak wabah dan menggambar rupanya menolak kejahatan.
claims.quote: 貘者，象鼻犀目，牛尾虎足，生南方山谷中。寢其皮辟瘟，圖其形辟邪。

claims.statement: Bai Juyi writes that, according to the Shanhaijing, this beast eats iron and copper and nothing else.
claims.statement_id: Bai Juyi menulis bahwa menurut Shanhaijing binatang ini memakan besi dan tembaga dan tidak makan hal lain.
claims.quote: 寢其皮辟瘟，圖其形辟邪。予舊病頭風，每寢息，常以小屏衛其首，適遇畫工，偶令寫之。按《山海經》，此獸食鐵與銅，不食他物。

claims.statement: In the hymn itself, Bai Juyi calls the mo a marvellous beast born in the southern land that eats nothing but iron.
claims.statement_id: Dalam baris pujiannya, Bai Juyi menyebut Mo sebagai binatang ajaib dari negeri selatan yang tidak makan selain besi.
claims.quote: 邈哉奇獸，生於南國。其名曰貘，非鐵不食。昔在上古，人心忠質。

claims.statement: The Nine-Eared Hound belongs to the mythology of the Leizhou Peninsula.
claims.statement_id: Anjing Bertelinga Sembilan berasal dari mitologi Semenanjung Leizhou.
claims.quote: The Nine-Eared Hound (Chinese: 九耳犬) is a legendary dog from the mythology of Leizhou Peninsula. In the earliest extant version of the myth, collected in Taiping Guangji (978) and dating from the Tang dynasty (618–907), it had twelve instead of nine ears.

claims.statement: The earliest surviving version in Taiping Guangji gives the hound twelve ears.
claims.statement_id: Versi awal yang bertahan dalam Taiping Guangji menyebut dua belas telinga.
claims.quote: The Nine-Eared Hound (Chinese: 九耳犬) is a legendary dog from the mythology of Leizhou Peninsula. In the earliest extant version of the myth, collected in Taiping Guangji (978) and dating from the Tang dynasty (618–907), it had twelve instead of nine ears.

claims.statement: Yuan Mei includes one version in chapter 12 of What the Master Would Not Discuss.
claims.statement_id: Yuan Mei menempatkan salah satu versi kisahnya dalam bab 12 What the Master Would Not Discuss.
claims.quote: One version of the myth is found in Chapter 12 of Yuan Mei's What the Master Would Not Discuss (1788). The Nine-Eared Hound belonged to a hunter surnamed Chen (陳). Before each hunting trip, the number of its ears that quivered accurately predicted the number of prey. One time, all its nine ears quivered but they did not catch anything all morning.

claims.statement: The dog belongs to a hunter named Chen and predicts the number of prey through its quivering ears.
claims.statement_id: Anjing milik pemburu bermarga Chen ini meramalkan jumlah buruan melalui telinganya yang bergerak.
claims.quote: One version of the myth is found in Chapter 12 of Yuan Mei's What the Master Would Not Discuss (1788). The Nine-Eared Hound belonged to a hunter surnamed Chen (陳). Before each hunting trip, the number of its ears that quivered accurately predicted the number of prey. One time, all its nine ears quivered but they did not catch anything all morning.

claims.statement: The dog leads Chen to a large egg that later opens during a thunderstorm to reveal a baby.
claims.statement_id: Anjing tersebut membawa Chen kepada telur besar yang kemudian menetas menjadi bayi ketika terjadi badai.
claims.quote: Chen found a huge egg and brought it home. The next day, during a thunderstorm, the egg cracked open, revealing a lovely baby.

claims.statement: In another version the child is named Chen Wenyu, associated with the God of Thunder in Leizhou.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi lain, bayi itu bernama Chen Wenyu, yang dikaitkan dengan Dewa Guntur di Leizhou.
claims.quote: In another version, the baby had the characters "Leizhou" written in one palm and the characters "Chen Wenyu" written in the other, and Chen Wenyu became his name. Even today, the God of Thunder is known as Chen Wenyu in Leizhou, where local people of the Chen surname claimed descent from him. In another local legend, the dog became the companion for the God of Thunder.

claims.statement: The Taiping Guangji records a man of the Lei region who kept a hunting dog with twelve ears; before a hunt, the number of ears that moved was taken as the number of animals to be caught.
claims.statement_id: Taiping Guangji mencatat seorang penduduk daerah Lei yang memelihara anjing pemburu berdua belas telinga; sebelum berburu, jumlah telinga yang bergerak dibaca sebagai jumlah buruan.
claims.quote: 又云：「嘗有雷民，畜畋犬，其耳十二。每將獵，必笞犬，以耳動為獲數。

claims.statement: One day all of the dog's ears moved; afterwards it no longer chased game and howled by the sea.
claims.statement_id: Pada suatu hari semua telinga anjing itu bergerak; setelah itu ia tidak lagi mengejar binatang buruan dan menggonggong di tepi laut.
claims.quote: 以耳動為獲數。 ... 一日，諸耳畢動。既獵，不復逐獸。至海旁測中嗥鳴。郡人視之

claims.statement: In this version the eggs brought home broke open after a storm and left their shells; the people of the commandery divided the shells and made offerings to them at set times, and holding a shell marked a prominent clan.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi ini, telur-telur yang dibawa pulang pecah setelah badai dan meninggalkan cangkangnya; penduduk setempat membagi cangkang itu, memujanya pada waktu-waktu tertentu, dan memiliki cangkang dianggap tanda keluarga terpandang.
claims.quote: 後忽風雨，若出自室。既霽就視，卵破而遺甲存焉。後郡人分其卵甲，歲時祀奠，至今以獲得遺甲為豪族。

claims.statement: The Guangdong Xinyu says that Chen Kun of Leizhou, who had no son and made his living by hunting, kept a very efficacious nine-eared dog; each ear that moved meant one animal caught.
claims.statement_id: Guangdong Xinyu menulis bahwa Chen Kun dari Leizhou, yang tidak punya anak dan berprofesi pemburu, memiliki anjing bertelinga sembilan yang sangat sakti; satu telinga yang bergerak berarti satu buruan.
claims.quote: 陳時雷州人陳鉷無子，其業捕獵，家有九耳犬甚靈。凡將獵，卜諸犬耳。一耳動，則獲一獸，動多則三四耳，少則一二耳。

claims.statement: One day all nine ears moved and the dog kept circling a thicket; Chen Kun found a huge egg and took it home, and in a thunderstorm it opened to reveal a boy with the characters for Lei and Zhou written on his hands.
claims.statement_id: Pada suatu hari kesembilan telinga bergerak dan anjing itu terus mengitari semak berduri; Chen Kun menemukan telur besar, membawanya pulang, dan ketika badai petir datang telur itu terbuka menjadi seorang laki-laki yang di telapak tangannya tertulis aksara untuk Lei dan Zhou.
claims.quote: 一日出獵，而九耳俱動，鉷大喜，以為必多得獸矣。既之野，有叢棘一區，九耳犬圍繞不去。異之，得一巨卵徑尺，攜以歸，雷雨暴作，卵開，乃一男子，其手有文，左曰雷，右曰州

claims.statement: The Scorpion Demoness is an antagonist in the classic novel Journey to the West.
claims.statement_id: Siluman Kalajengking adalah antagonis dalam novel klasik Journey to the West.
claims.quote: Scorpion Demoness, also known as Xiezijing (Chinese: 蝎子精; pinyin: Xiēzǐ jīng), is a major antagonist from the 16th-century Chinese classic novel Journey to the West and its media adaptations. Her true form is a giant scorpion as large as a pipa. In the narrative, the Scorpion Demoness stands out as the sole character capable of harming both the Buddha and Sun Wukong.

claims.statement: The character's true form is a giant scorpion the size of a pipa.
claims.statement_id: Wujud asli tokoh ini adalah kalajengking raksasa sebesar pipa.
claims.quote: Scorpion Demoness, also known as Xiezijing (Chinese: 蝎子精; pinyin: Xiēzǐ jīng), is a major antagonist from the 16th-century Chinese classic novel Journey to the West and its media adaptations. Her true form is a giant scorpion as large as a pipa. In the narrative, the Scorpion Demoness stands out as the sole character capable of harming both the Buddha and Sun Wukong.

claims.statement: Her tail sting can injure both the Buddha and Sun Wukong in the story.
claims.statement_id: Sengatan ekornya mampu melukai Buddha dan Sun Wukong dalam cerita.
claims.quote: Scorpion Demoness, also known as Xiezijing (Chinese: 蝎子精; pinyin: Xiēzǐ jīng), is a major antagonist from the 16th-century Chinese classic novel Journey to the West and its media adaptations. Her true form is a giant scorpion as large as a pipa. In the narrative, the Scorpion Demoness stands out as the sole character capable of harming both the Buddha and Sun Wukong.

claims.statement: She lives in Pipa Cave on Venom Mountain near the Women's Kingdom.
claims.statement_id: Ia menghuni Pipa Cave di Venom Mountain, dekat Women's Kingdom.
claims.quote: The Scorpion Demoness resides in Pipa Cave (琵琶洞) on Venom Mountain (毒敵山), near the Women's Kingdom. When Tang Sanzang and his disciples are about to leave the Women's Kingdom, the scorpion demoness suddenly appears, abducting Sanzang to her cave. There, she attempts to seduce and persuade him into marriage, leading him into the bridal suite she has prepared.

claims.statement: She abducts Tang Sanzang and tries to persuade him to marry her.
claims.statement_id: Ia menculik Tang Sanzang dan berusaha membujuknya menikah.
claims.quote: The Scorpion Demoness resides in Pipa Cave (琵琶洞) on Venom Mountain (毒敵山), near the Women's Kingdom. When Tang Sanzang and his disciples are about to leave the Women's Kingdom, the scorpion demoness suddenly appears, abducting Sanzang to her cave. There, she attempts to seduce and persuade him into marriage, leading him into the bridal suite she has prepared.

claims.statement: Maori Xingguan defeats her by becoming a giant rooster with two combs.
claims.statement_id: Maori Xingguan menundukkannya dengan berubah menjadi ayam jantan raksasa berjengger dua.
claims.quote: Eventually, Maori Xingguan subdues the demoness by transforming into a giant rooster with two combs.

claims.statement: In the novel, the Bodhisattva explains that the demoness's three-pronged fork is really a pair of pincers, that the painful sting comes from a hook on her tail called "daoma du" (horse-felling venom), and that her true body is a scorpion spirit.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, sang Bodhisattva menjelaskan bahwa garpu bermata tiga milik siluman itu sebenarnya sepasang capit, bahwa tusukan yang menyakitkan berasal dari kait di ujung ekor yang disebut "daoma du", dan bahwa wujud aslinya adalah siluman kalajengking.
claims.quote: 菩薩道：「這妖精十分利害。他那三股叉是生成的兩隻鉗腳。扎人痛者，是尾上一個鉤子，喚做倒馬毒。本身是個蝎子精。

claims.statement: According to the Bodhisattva in the novel, the demoness once listened to the Buddha discuss the sutras at the Temple 雷音寺 (Leiyin); when Rulai (如來) pushed her, she turned her hook and stung the middle thumb of Rulai's left hand, causing him unbearable pain.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sang Bodhisattva dalam novel, siluman itu pernah mendengarkan Buddha berbicara tentang sutra di Kuil 雷音寺 (Leiyin); ketika Rulai (如來) mendorongnya, ia memutar kaitnya dan menusuk ibu jari tengah tangan kiri Rulai hingga sakit tak tertahankan.
claims.quote: 他前者在雷音寺聽佛談經，如來見了，不合用手推他一把，他就轉過鉤子，把如來左手中拇指上扎了一下。如來也疼難禁，即著金剛拿他。

claims.statement: Sun Wukong (行者) tells the star official that his master is in trouble in the cave 琵琶洞 on the mountain 毒敵山 in the country 西梁國.
claims.statement_id: Sun Wukong (行者) memberi tahu sang penguasa bintang bahwa gurunya sedang dalam kesulitan di Gua 琵琶洞 di Gunung 毒敵山 di negeri 西梁國.
claims.quote: 那星官斂雲霧整束朝衣，停執事分開左右，上前作禮道：「大聖何來？」行者道：「專來拜煩救師父一難。」星官道：「何難？在何地方？」行者道：「在西梁國毒敵山琵琶洞。」

claims.statement: In the novel the star official appears as a great double-crested rooster about six or seven chi (尺) tall; when it crows, the demoness reveals her true form, a scorpion as big as a pipa, and after a second crow her body goes limp and she dies.
claims.statement_id: Di novel itu, sang penguasa bintang tampil sebagai ayam jantan besar berjengger ganda setinggi sekitar enam atau tujuh chi (尺); ketika ia berkokok, siluman itu menampakkan wujud aslinya, kalajengking sebesar pipa, lalu lemas dan mati setelah kokokan kedua.
claims.quote: 原來是一隻雙冠子大公雞，昂起頭來，約有六七尺高，對著妖怪叫了一聲。那怪即時就現了本相，原來是個琵琶來大小的一個蝎子精。這星官再叫一聲，那怪渾身酥軟，死在坡前。

claims.statement: Shuzi, also called Shūji, is an ancient Chinese legendary animal resembling a large tiger.
claims.statement_id: Shuzi atau Shūji adalah hewan legendaris Tiongkok kuno menyerupai harimau besar.
claims.quote: 酋耳（しゅうじ）とは古代中国の伝説上の生き物。大きな虎のようなすがたをしているとされる。

claims.statement: It is described with a very large body and a long tail.
claims.statement_id: Tubuh dan ekornya digambarkan sangat besar serta panjang.
claims.quote: 見た目は虎のようで体はとても大きく尾もとても長いが、決して生きた獣を捕食しないという。ただし、虎や豹を目にすると態度は変わり必ず襲ってそれを殺すと伝えられていた。狩り捕った虎や豹は食べるとされる場合もあるが、酋耳は狩るのみでその肉を食べたりはしないとも語られる。

claims.statement: It generally avoids hunting living animals but attacks tigers and leopards.
claims.statement_id: Ia umumnya tidak memburu hewan hidup, tetapi menyerang harimau dan macan tutul.
claims.quote: 見た目は虎のようで体はとても大きく尾もとても長いが、決して生きた獣を捕食しないという。ただし、虎や豹を目にすると態度は変わり必ず襲ってそれを殺すと伝えられていた。狩り捕った虎や豹は食べるとされる場合もあるが、酋耳は狩るのみでその肉を食べたりはしないとも語られる。

claims.statement: Versions differ over whether it eats the animals it kills.
claims.statement_id: Versi cerita berbeda mengenai apakah hasil buruannya dimakan.
claims.quote: 見た目は虎のようで体はとても大きく尾もとても長いが、決して生きた獣を捕食しないという。ただし、虎や豹を目にすると態度は変わり必ず襲ってそれを殺すと伝えられていた。狩り捕った虎や豹は食べるとされる場合もあるが、酋耳は狩るのみでその肉を食べたりはしないとも語られる。

claims.statement: The Sancai Tuhui connects its appearance with a ruler's authority extending to the surrounding peoples.
claims.statement_id: Sancai Tuhui menghubungkan kemunculannya dengan kewibawaan penguasa yang meluas ke wilayah luar.
claims.quote: 『三才図会』では、王者の威勢が四夷に及んだ際に世に出現する獣であるとされている。『逸周書』「王会」の解では各地から贈られて来ためずらしい禽獣魚介のうちのひとつとして贈られていることが記されているが、これを献上している央林（『三才図会』では「英林山」とされている）については西の方角に属する地である以外にはあまり詳しく分かっていない。

claims.statement: Shuzi is sometimes identified with Zouyu, allowing their attributes to overlap.
claims.statement_id: Shuzi kadang disamakan dengan Zouyu sehingga ciri kedua makhluk saling bercampur.
claims.quote: 同様に獣を捕食しないとされる中国に伝わる霊獣には騶虞（すうぐ）というものもあり、そちらは仁獣とされている。性質が似通っていることから同じ霊獣と見られたり、混同が行われて来ており「虎や豹を見ると狩るが、食べない」と言われたりする点や「長い尾が特徴である」とされる点など互いの属性がまじりつつ伝わっている面もある。

claims.statement: The 《三才圖會》 passage in the Gujin tushu jicheng says the 酋耳 lives on Mount 英林山, was once presented in the time of King Cheng of Zhou, has a tail longer than its body, eats tigers and leopards, and appears when a ruler's might reaches the four barbarian quarters.
claims.statement_id: Kutipan dari 《三才圖會》 dalam Gujin Tushu Jicheng menyebut 酋耳 ada di gunung 英林山, pernah dipersembahkan pada masa Raja Cheng dari Zhou, berekor lebih panjang dari tubuhnya, memakan harimau dan macan tutul, dan muncul ketika wibawa raja menjangkau empat penjuru bangsa asing.
claims.quote: 英林山有酋耳，周成王時曾獻之。尾長於身，食虎豹。 王者威及四夷，則此獸至。

claims.statement: The 《汲冢周書》, chapter 王會解, as quoted, says the 酋耳 has a body like a tiger or leopard, a tail of three chi, and eats tigers and leopards.
claims.statement_id: Kitab 《汲冢周書》 bab 王會解, sebagaimana dikutip, menyebut 酋耳 berbadan seperti harimau atau macan tutul, berekor tiga chi, dan memakan harimau serta macan tutul.
claims.quote: 《汲冢周書》王會解：「史林以酋耳。」酋耳者，身若虎豹，尾 長三尺，其身食虎豹。

claims.statement: According to 《朝野僉載》, in the time of the Empress (天后) a huge tiger-like beast chased and killed a tiger without eating its flesh; when checked against the 瑞圖 (auspicious omen illustrations), it was identified as a 酋耳.
claims.statement_id: Menurut 《朝野僉載》, pada masa Permaisuri (天后) seekor binatang sangat besar mirip harimau mengejar dan membunuh seekor harimau tanpa memakan dagingnya; setelah dicocokkan dengan 瑞圖 (gambar pertanda baik), binatang itu dinyatakan sebagai 酋耳.
claims.quote: 天后時，涪州龍虎界多虎暴。有一獸似虎 而絕大，日正午，逐一虎直入人家，噬殺之，不食其肉。 自是縣界不復有虎矣。錄奏檢瑞圖，乃酋耳。

claims.statement: A passage from the 《冊府元龜》 records that in the third month of the 24th year of Kaiyuan (開元二十四年) an auspicious beast was captured; the 酋耳 was tiger-like, had a tail longer than its body, leopard markings, and could eat tigers.
claims.statement_id: Kutipan dari 《冊府元龜》 mencatat bahwa pada bulan ketiga tahun 開元二十四 seekor binatang pertanda baik ditangkap; 酋耳 itu berbentuk seperti harimau, berekor lebih panjang dari tubuh, bercorak macan tutul, dan mampu memakan harimau.
claims.quote: 《冊府元龜》：「開元二十四年三月，獲瑞獸，酋耳形類虎， 尾長於身，有豹文，能食虎。」

claims.statement: Tenghuang is an auspicious creature in Chinese mythology.
claims.statement_id: Tenghuang merupakan makhluk pembawa pertanda baik dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: Tenghuang (Chinese: 騰黃; also known by various names as Chenghuang, Feihuang, Guhuangm, and Cuihuang) is a mythological creature which is symbol of auspiciousness in Chinese mythology. It is mentioned in the Shanhaijing.

claims.statement: Tenghuang is mentioned in the Shanhaijing.
claims.statement_id: Artikel menyebut kemunculannya dalam Shan Hai Jing.
claims.quote: It is mentioned in the Shanhaijing.

claims.statement: One version describes a foxlike beast with wings and dragonlike horns on its back.
claims.statement_id: Satu versi menggambarkannya seperti rubah, dengan sayap dan tanduk naga di punggung.
claims.quote: There are two versions of what Tenghuang looked like. It is said to be a beast like a fox, with wings and horns like a dragon on its back. The life span of those who ride it can grow to two thousand years. Another claim states that it has the appearance of a horse.

claims.statement: Another version gives Tenghuang a horse's appearance; its rider is said to gain a lifespan of two thousand years.
claims.statement_id: Versi lain memberi Tenghuang rupa kuda; penunggangnya dikatakan memperoleh umur dua ribu tahun.
claims.quote: There are two versions of what Tenghuang looked like. It is said to be a beast like a fox, with wings and horns like a dragon on its back. The life span of those who ride it can grow to two thousand years. Another claim states that it has the appearance of a horse.

claims.statement: Expressions referring to riding Tenghuang describe rising in status or reputation.
claims.statement_id: Ungkapan yang mengacu pada menunggang Tenghuang dipakai untuk kenaikan kedudukan atau reputasi.
claims.quote: There is an idiom in Chinese, "Flying the Yellow Tengda" (飛黃騰達) or "Riding on the Tenghuang". It is used to describe a person ascending and gaining a high position or reputation.

claims.statement: The Shanhaijing (Overseas West section) names the 乘黃 (Chenghuang) in the land of the 白民: it looks like a fox, has horns on its back, and whoever rides it lives two thousand years.
claims.statement_id: Shanhaijing (Haiwai Xi Jing) menyebut 乘黃 (Chenghuang) di Negeri 白民: bentuknya seperti rubah, di punggungnya ada tanduk, dan yang menungganginya berumur dua ribu tahun.
claims.quote: 白民之國在龍魚北，白身披髮。有乘黃，其狀如狐，其背上有角，乘之壽二千歲。

claims.statement: The compilation 名馬記 quotes the 《淮南子》 and Gao You's commentary: the 飛黃 (Feihuang) is like a fox with horns on its back, covers ten thousand li a day, and its rider lives three thousand years.
claims.statement_id: Himpunan 名馬記 mengutip 《淮南子》 dan komentar Gao You: 飛黃 (Feihuang) seperti rubah dengan tanduk di punggung, berlari sepuluh ribu li sehari, dan penunggangnya berumur tiga ribu tahun.
claims.quote: 《淮南子》曰：黃帝治天下，飛黃服皂。高誘曰：飛黃如狐，背有角，日行萬里，乘之壽三千歲。

claims.statement: A passage from the 《瑞應圖》 in the 名馬記 calls the 騰黃 a divine yellow horse that arrives when a ruler governs the four quarters through virtue, also named 吉光, whose rider lives three thousand years and which never dies.
claims.statement_id: Kutipan dari 《瑞應圖》 dalam 名馬記 menyebut 騰黃 sebagai kuda ajaib berwarna kuning yang datang ketika penguasa memerintah keempat penjuru dengan kebajikan, juga dinamai 吉光, yang penunggangnya berumur tiga ribu tahun dan kuda itu tak punya masa mati.
claims.quote: 《瑞應圖》曰：騰黃者，神馬也，其色黃，王者德御四方則至。一名吉光，乘之壽三千歲，此馬無死時。

claims.statement: According to Ying Shao (應劭), quoted in the 名馬記, the 乘黃 has dragon wings and a horse's body, and the Yellow Emperor (黃帝) rode it and became an immortal; the 《瑞應圖》 adds that the 乘黃 appears when a ruler's carriage and dress follow proper rules.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Ying Shao (應劭) yang dikutip dalam 名馬記, 乘黃 bersayap naga dan bertubuh kuda, dan Kaisar Kuning (黃帝) menungganginya lalu menjadi dewa; 《瑞應圖》 menambahkan bahwa 乘黃 muncul ketika kereta dan busana penguasa sesuai aturan.
claims.quote: 應劭曰：乘黃，龍翼馬身，黃帝乘而仙。 《瑞應圖》曰：乘黃者，王者輿服有度則出。

claims.statement: The Nine-tailed Turtle is a legendary animal from China.
claims.statement_id: Kura-kura Berekor Sembilan adalah hewan legendaris Tiongkok.
claims.quote: The Nine-tailed turtle (traditional Chinese: 九尾龜; simplified Chinese: 九尾龟) is a legendary Chinese turtle.

claims.statement: The name Turtle of Nine Provinces appears in Chu Shaosun's supplement to the Records of the Grand Historian.
claims.statement_id: Nama Turtle of Nine Provinces muncul dalam tambahan Chu Shaosun pada Records of the Grand Historian.
claims.quote: In an appended supplement to Records of the Grand Historian, the Han dynasty scholar Chu Shaosun (104?–30 BC) mentioned eight famous turtles particularly suitable for plastromancy or turtle shell divination, one being called the "Turtle of Nine Provinces" (九州龜).

claims.statement: In folklore, Turtle of Nine Provinces develops into Turtle of Nine Tails.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat, Turtle of Nine Provinces berkembang menjadi Turtle of Nine Tails.
claims.quote: Over time "Turtle of Nine Provinces" became "Turtle of Nine Tails" in folklore. According to one source, it takes a turtle three thousand years to grow another tail.

claims.statement: Two stories from imperial China are interpreted as encouraging the release of living turtles.
claims.statement_id: Dua kisah dari Tiongkok kekaisaran dipahami sebagai dukungan terhadap pelepasan kura-kura hidup.
claims.quote: Two extant stories from imperial China both appear to advocate for the life release of nine-tailed turtles.

claims.statement: Hong Mai's Yijian Zhi includes a turtle appearing during the siege of Yingtian in 1126.
claims.statement_id: Yijian Zhi karya Hong Mai memuat kisah kura-kura yang muncul ketika Yingtian dikepung pada 1126.
claims.quote: According to a story compiled by Hong Mai (1123–1202) in his Yijian Zhi, during the Jin–Song Wars of 1126, when the Song "southern capital" Yingtian Prefecture (modern Shangqiu) was under siege, a huge nine-tailed turtle appeared in the city. It was described as being three chi tall, "as big as a wheel", with nine bony tails and a yellow, waxy carapace.

claims.statement: The turtle in that story is wheel sized, with nine bony tails and a yellow waxy carapace.
claims.statement_id: Kura-kura dalam kisah itu sebesar roda, dengan sembilan ekor bertulang dan karapas kuning seperti lilin.
claims.quote: According to a story compiled by Hong Mai (1123–1202) in his Yijian Zhi, during the Jin–Song Wars of 1126, when the Song "southern capital" Yingtian Prefecture (modern Shangqiu) was under siege, a huge nine-tailed turtle appeared in the city. It was described as being three chi tall, "as big as a wheel", with nine bony tails and a yellow, waxy carapace.

claims.statement: The chapter on turtles and divination in the 《史記》 lists eight named turtles, the seventh being the 九州龜 (Turtle of Nine Provinces), and says that whoever obtains a named turtle will gain wealth and a very rich household.
claims.statement_id: Bab tentang kura-kura dan ramalan dalam 《史記》 mendaftar delapan kura-kura bernama, yang ketujuh adalah 九州龜 (kura-kura Sembilan Provinsi), dan menyebut bahwa orang yang mendapatkan kura-kura bernama akan memperoleh harta dan menjadi sangat kaya.
claims.quote: 記曰：「能得名龜者，財物歸之，家必大富至千萬。」一曰「北斗龜」，二曰「南辰龜」，三曰「五星龜」，四曰「八風龜」，五曰「二十八宿龜」，六曰「日月龜」，七曰「九州龜」，八曰「玉龜」：凡八名龜。

claims.statement: In the 《庚巳編》, a butcher surnamed Wang of Haining and his son buy a large turtle from a fisherman and tie it under a pillar to make soup of it; a merchant from Jiangyou staying nearby asks his landlord to redeem it for a thousand coins.
claims.statement_id: Dalam 《庚巳編》, seorang penjagal bermarga Wang di Haining dan putranya membeli kura-kura besar dari nelayan dan mengikatnya di bawah tiang untuk dijadikan sup; seorang pedagang dari Jiangyou yang tinggal di dekat situ meminta penginapnya menebusnya dengan seribu uang.
claims.quote: 海寧百姓王屠與其子出行，遇漁父持巨龜，徑可尺餘，買歸係著柱下，將羹之。鄰居有江右商人見之，告其邸翁，請以千錢贖焉。

claims.statement: The merchant calls it a 九尾龜, a divine creature he wants to buy and release; when he steps on its shell, four small tails appear on each side of the large tail. Wang refuses to sell it and cooks it into soup that he and his son eat.
claims.statement_id: Pedagang itu menyebut kura-kura tersebut 九尾龜, makhluk gaib yang ingin ia beli untuk dilepas; ketika ia menginjak cangkangnya, tampak empat ekor kecil di tiap sisi ekor besar. Wang menolak menjualnya dan memasaknya menjadi sup untuk dimakan bersama putranya.
claims.quote: 商曰：「此九尾龜，神物也，欲買放去。 ... 商踏龜背，其尾之兩旁露小尾各四，便持錢乞王，王不肯，遂烹作羹，父子共啖。

claims.statement: That evening a flood came in from the sea and floated the beds; next day the landlord broke open their door and found only clothes and bedding on the bed, the father and son gone. Some said they were taken and killed by the water palace for harming a divine turtle.
claims.statement_id: Malam itu air bah datang dari laut hingga tempat tidur mengapung; keesokan harinya sang penginap membongkar pintu dan hanya menemukan pakaian dan selimut di ranjang, sementara ayah dan anak itu hilang. Orang berkata mereka dibawa dan dibunuh penguasa air karena mencelakai kura-kura ajaib.
claims.quote: 是夕，大水自海中來，平地高三尺許，牀榻盡浮，十餘刻始退。及明午，翁怪王屠父子不起，坏戶入視之，但見衣衾在牀，父子都不知去向。人或云：害神龜，為水府攝去殺卻也。

claims.statement: Three-legged turtles and softshell turtles are mythical animals from China.
claims.statement_id: Kura-kura dan labi-labi berkaki tiga merupakan hewan mitos dari Tiongkok.
claims.quote: Three-legged turtle (simplified Chinese: 三足龟; traditional Chinese: 三足龜; pinyin: Sānzúguī) and Three-legged softshell turtle (simplified Chinese: 三足鳖; traditional Chinese: 三足鱉; pinyin: Sānzúbiē) are mythical turtles from China.

claims.statement: The Erya names the hard shelled turtle Fen and the softshell turtle Nai.
claims.statement_id: Erya memberi nama Fen untuk kura-kura bercangkang keras dan Nai untuk labi-labi.
claims.quote: According to the ancient dictionary Erya, the former (pertaining to hardshell turtles including tortoises) is properly called Fen (simplified Chinese: 贲; traditional Chinese: 賁; pinyin: Fén), and the latter, Nai (Chinese: 能; pinyin: Nái).

claims.statement: A translation of the Shan Hai Jing places three-footed turtles in River Mad on Mount Bigbitter.
claims.statement_id: Terjemahan Shan Hai Jing menyebut kura-kura berkaki tiga di River Mad pada Mount Bigbitter.
claims.quote: ...On the south face of Mount Bigbitter the River Mad rises and flows southwest to empty into the River Person. Three-footed turtles are numerous in the River Mad. Those who eat it won't have a serious illness, and it can be taken to cure a swelling.

claims.statement: Another passage places three-footed softshell turtles with branching tails in River Trailer.
claims.statement_id: Kisah lain menempatkan labi-labi berkaki tiga dengan ekor bercabang di River Trailer.
claims.quote: ...The River Trailer rises on its summit and runs a hidden course to its base. This river contains many three-footed [softshell] turtles with a branching tail. If you eat it, you won't succumb to the plague of the malign force.

claims.statement: The annotation to the Erya quotes the 《山海經》: three-legged softshell turtles are plentiful on Mount 從山 and three-legged turtles on Mount 大苦山; it adds that a pond on Mount 君山 in Yangxian County (吳興郡陽羨縣) yields three-legged softshell turtles and also six-eyed turtles.
claims.statement_id: Catatan pada Erya mengutip 《山海經》: banyak labi-labi berkaki tiga di gunung 從山 dan kura-kura berkaki tiga di gunung 大苦山; catatan itu menambahkan bahwa di kolam di gunung 君山 di Kabupaten 陽羨 (Wuxing) muncul labi-labi berkaki tiga dan juga kura-kura bermata enam.
claims.quote: 《山海經》曰：從山多三足鱉，大苦山多三足龜。今吳興郡陽羨縣君山上有池，池中出三足鱉，又有六眼龜。

claims.statement: The commentary to the Erya explains that softshell turtles and turtles ordinarily have four feet, so the three-footed ones are given different names: 能 for the softshell turtle and 賁 for the turtle.
claims.statement_id: Komentar pada Erya menjelaskan bahwa labi-labi dan kura-kura umumnya berkaki empat, sehingga yang berkaki tiga diberi nama berbeda: 能 untuk labi-labi dan 賁 untuk kura-kura.
claims.quote: 鱉、龜皆四足，三足者異，故異其名。鱉之三足者名能，龜之三足者名賁也。

claims.statement: The 《庚巳編》 tells of a commoner of 太倉州 who bought a three-legged softshell turtle from a fisherman and had his wife cook it; after he ate it, his wife found only a lock of hair and his clothes on the ground, as if he had shed his form.
claims.statement_id: Dalam 《庚巳編》 diceritakan seorang warga 太倉州 membeli labi-labi berkaki tiga dari nelayan dan istrinya memasaknya; setelah ia memakannya sendiri, sang istri masuk dan hanya menemukan seuntai rambut serta pakaian suaminya di lantai, seolah ia telah meluruhkan wujudnya.
claims.quote: 庚午夏，太倉州有百姓道見漁者，持一鱉而三足，買歸令婦炰之。既熟，呼婦共餐，婦不欲食，出坐門外。久之不聞其夫聲，入視已失所在，地上止存發一縷，衣服冠履，事事皆在，如蛻形者。

claims.statement: The fishermen in the tale say that when ordered to catch a three-legged softshell turtle they first netted something very heavy, a lump of flesh shaped like a person with all facial features but no hands or feet, wriggling with closed eyes, and threw it back into the water.
claims.statement_id: Para nelayan dalam kisah itu mengatakan bahwa ketika diperintahkan menangkap labi-labi berkaki tiga, mereka lebih dulu menjaring benda yang sangat berat berupa gumpalan daging berbentuk manusia, berwajah lengkap tetapi tanpa tangan dan kaki, bergerak-gerak dengan mata terpejam, lalu melemparnya kembali ke air.

claims.statement: Xuangui is a fabulous turtle in Chinese legend with a bird's head and a snake's tail.
claims.statement_id: Xuangui adalah kura-kura ajaib dalam legenda Tiongkok, dengan kepala burung dan ekor ular.

claims.statement_id: Boyi adalah makhluk mirip domba dengan sembilan ekor dan empat telinga dalam Shan Hai Jing.
claims.quote: 猼訑，異獸也，出基山。其狀如羊，九尾四耳，其目在背。佩之不畏。

claims.statement: The mountain where Boyi is recorded has jade on its southern side and unusual trees on its northern side.

claims.statement: Xie Duan leaves at cockcrow, sneaks back early and peeks from outside the fence; he sees a young woman come out of the urn and light the fire at the stove, and when he goes in to the urn he sees only the snail's shell.
claims.statement_id: Xie Duan pergi saat ayam berkokok lalu diam-diam pulang pagi-pagi dan mengintip dari balik pagar; ia melihat seorang gadis keluar dari guci dan menyalakan api di tungku, dan ketika ia masuk ke dekat guci, ia hanya menemukan cangkang siput.
claims.quote: 後以雞鳴出去，平早潛歸，於籬外竊窺其家中。見一少女，從甕中出，至灶下燃火。端便入門，逕至甕所，視螺，但見殼。

claims.statement: She answers that she is the 白水素女 of the Heavenly River; the Celestial Emperor (天帝) pitied Xie Duan, orphaned young yet self-disciplined, and sent her to keep his house and cook for a time, to leave once ten years had made him rich and married.
claims.statement_id: Gadis itu menjawab bahwa ia adalah 白水素女 dari Sungai Langit; Kaisar Langit (天帝) iba pada Xie Duan yang yatim dan menjaga diri, sehingga mengutusnya sementara menjaga rumah dan memasak, dan setelah sepuluh tahun yang membuatnya kaya dan beristri, ia akan pergi.
claims.quote: 答曰：「我天漢中白水素女也。天帝哀卿少孤，恭慎自守，故使我權相為守舍炊烹。十年之中，使卿居富得婦，自當還去。

claims.statement: She leaves her shell for storing rice so he would never lack, refuses to stay and departs with sudden wind and rain; Xie Duan sets up a spirit seat and offers sacrifices in season, lives in comfort, is married to a local girl and later holds office; the text says the shrine 素女祠 on the road is that shrine.
claims.statement_id: Ia meninggalkan cangkangnya untuk menyimpan beras agar tidak pernah kekurangan, menolak tetap tinggal, dan pergi bersama angin dan hujan; Xie Duan mendirikan altar dan memberi persembahan pada waktunya, hidup berkecukupan, menikah dengan gadis desa, dan kemudian menjabat; teks itu menyebut kuil 素女祠 di jalan sebagai kuil tersebut.
claims.quote: 留此殼去，以貯米穀，常可不乏。端請留，終不肯。時天忽風雨，翕然而去。端為立神座，時節祭祀。居常饒足，不致大富耳。於是鄉人以女妻之，後仕至令長云。今道中素女祠是也。

claims.statement: The Southern section of the Shanhaijing says that on Mount 禱過之山 there is a bird shaped like a 鵁 with a white head (one version writes 手 for 首), three feet and a human face, named 瞿如, whose cry calls its own name; an annotation says the 鵁 resembles a duck but is smaller, with its legs near the tail.

claims.statement: Jiguang is an auspicious fabulous animal in Chinese mythology.
claims.statement_id: Jiguang adalah hewan ajaib pembawa keberuntungan dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: 吉光，又稱吉良、澤馬，是中國神話傳說中的神獸，是吉祥的象徵。常與騰黃混淆在一起。

claims.statement: One description gives it the form of a patterned white horse with a red mane, born in a great marsh.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu uraian memberinya bentuk kuda putih berpola dengan surai merah yang lahir di rawa besar.
claims.quote: 吉光被認為是一種馬，出生在大澤中，身體是白的，帶著花紋，但是鬃毛是紅的。

claims.statement: Jiguang is often confused with Tenghuang, while fox and horse forms differ between versions.
claims.statement_id: Jiguang kerap dicampur dengan Tenghuang, sementara bentuk rubah dan kuda berbeda menurut versinya.
claims.quote: 有人認為它就是騰黃。一種說法認為，騰黃長得像狐狸，是一種野獸，而吉光長得像馬；然而有些說法是反過來的。

claims.statement: The expression Jiguang pianyu uses a strand of its fur as a metaphor for rare relics or documents.
claims.statement_id: Ungkapan Jiguang pianyu memakai sehelai bulunya sebagai kiasan untuk peninggalan atau dokumen langka.
claims.quote: 因為吉光是極難得一見的神獸，因此民間有成語「吉光片羽」，以吉光的一絲獸毛，來形容某種極難得一見的文獻或是文物。

claims.statement: The compilation 名馬記 says the 澤馬 is also called 吉良 and quotes the 《山海經》: in the country 大封國 there is a patterned horse with a white body and red mane named 吉良, whose rider lives a thousand years.
claims.statement_id: Himpunan 名馬記 menyebut 澤馬 juga bernama 吉良 dan mengutip 《山海經》: di negeri 大封國 ada kuda berpola bertubuh putih dan bersurai merah bernama 吉良, yang penunggangnya berumur seribu tahun.
claims.quote: 澤馬，一曰吉良。《山海經》曰：大封國有文馬，縞身朱鬛，名曰吉良，乘之壽千歲。

claims.statement: A passage from the 《瑞應圖》 calls the 騰黃 a divine yellow horse that is also named 吉光, and whose rider lives three thousand years.
claims.statement_id: Kutipan dari 《瑞應圖》 menyebut 騰黃 sebagai kuda ajaib berwarna kuning yang juga bernama 吉光, dan penunggangnya berumur tiga ribu tahun.
claims.quote: 《瑞應圖》曰：騰黃者，神馬也，其色黃，王者德御四方則至。一名吉光，乘之壽三千歲，此馬無死時。

claims.statement: The Baopuzi says that both the 騰黃 horse and the 吉光 beast live three thousand years, listed alongside the toad (蟾蜍) and the 騏驎, which live shorter lives.
claims.statement_id: Baopuzi menulis bahwa 騰黃之馬 dan 吉光之獸 sama-sama berumur tiga ribu tahun, disebut bersama katak (蟾蜍) dan 騏驎 yang berumur lebih pendek.
claims.quote: 蟾蜍壽三千歲，騏驎壽二千歲。騰黃之馬，吉光之獸，皆壽三千歲。

claims.statement: In the 《海內十洲記》 a 吉光 fur coat is presented to Emperor Wu (武帝) and stored in the outer treasury; the coat is yellow and said to belong to the divine-horse kind; it does not sink after days in water and does not scorch in fire.
claims.statement_id: Dalam 《海內十洲記》, 吉光毛裘 dipersembahkan kepada Kaisar Wu (武帝) dan disimpan di gudang luar; mantel bulu itu berwarna kuning dan dikatakan termasuk golongan kuda ajaib; mantel itu tidak tenggelam selama berhari-hari di air dan tidak hangus di api.
claims.quote: 献此膠四兩，吉光毛裘，武帝受以付外庫 ... 吉光毛裘黃色，盖神馬之類也。裘入水数日不沉，入火不焦。

claims.statement: Xiao is a name used for several Chinese creatures, including a long armed ape and a four winged bird.
claims.statement_id: Xiao adalah nama yang digunakan untuk beberapa makhluk Tiongkok, termasuk kera berlengan panjang dan burung bersayap empat.
claims.quote: In Chinese mythology, the xiao is the name of several creatures, including the xiao (Chinese: 囂; pinyin: xiāo; Wade–Giles: hsiao1) "a long-armed ape" or "a four-winged bird" and shanxiao (Chinese: 山魈; pinyin: shānxiāo) "mischievous, one-legged mountain spirit". Furthermore, some Western sources misspell and misconstrue the older romanization hsiao as "hsigo" [sic] "a flying monkey".

claims.statement: The word xiao includes meanings of noise and clamor.
claims.statement_id: Kata xiao mencakup makna gaduh atau bising.
claims.quote: means "noise; clamor; hubbub; haughty; proud; arrogant".

claims.statement: The Shan Hai Jing uses Xiao as a name for a river, a mountain, and two mythical creatures.
claims.statement_id: Shan Hai Jing memakai nama Xiao untuk sungai, gunung, dan dua makhluk mitos.
claims.quote: The Shanhaijing "Classic of Mountains and Seas" uses Xiao (some editions write the graphic variant 嚻) as the name of a river (囂水; Xiaoshui), a mountain (北囂之山; Beixiao zhi shan), and two mythical creatures.

claims.statement: One Xiao resembles an ape, has long arms, and is skilled at throwing things.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu Xiao menyerupai kera, berlengan panjang, dan mahir melempar benda.
claims.quote: Seventy leagues further west is a mountain called Mount Ewenext. … There is an animal on this mountain which looks like an ape, but it has longer arms and it is good at throwing things. Its name is the hubbub.

claims.statement: Another Xiao is described as a bird with four wings, one eye, and a dog's tail.
claims.statement_id: Xiao lain digambarkan sebagai burung dengan empat sayap, satu mata, dan ekor anjing.
claims.quote: Three hundred and fifty leagues further north is a mountain called Mount Bridgedrain. … There is a bird here which looks like the boastfather; it has four wings, one eye, and a dog's tail. Its name is the hubbub. It makes a noise like a magpie. If you eat it, it will cure a bellyache, and it is effective for indigestion.

claims.statement: Guo Pu's commentary records the variant Jufu in the passage comparing the Xiao bird with Kuafu.
claims.statement_id: Komentar Guo Pu menyebut varian Jufu pada bagian yang membandingkan burung Xiao dengan Kuafu.
claims.quote: Although this passage compares the Xiao bird with the humanoid Kuafu, the Shanhaijing commentary of Guo Pu (276–324) says an early textual version writes the Jufu (舉父), who is also described as yu "monkey; ape". The sub-commentary of Hao Yixing (郝懿行; 1757–1825) notes the association may be owing to the similar sounding names Kuafu and Jufu.

claims.statement: The Western section of the Shanhaijing describes a beast shaped like a 禺 (a kind of ape) with long arms, good at throwing, named 嚻; an annotation adds that it also appears in paintings of dreaded beasts and resembles a macaque throwing things.
claims.statement_id: Teks Shanhaijing bagian Barat menyebut binatang berbentuk seperti 禺 (sejenis kera) berlengan panjang yang pandai melempar bernama 嚻; catatan menambahkan bahwa ia juga ada dalam lukisan binatang menakutkan dan mirip monyet yang melempar benda.
claims.quote: 有獸焉，其狀如禺而長臂，善投，其名曰嚻〈亦在畏獸畫中，似獼猴投擲也〉。

claims.statement: The Northern section of the Shanhaijing describes a bird shaped like 夸父 with four wings, one eye and a dog's tail, named 嚻, with a cry like a magpie's; eating it cures bellyache and stops 衕.
claims.statement_id: Teks Shanhaijing bagian Utara menyebut burung berbentuk seperti 夸父 dengan empat sayap, satu mata, dan ekor anjing bernama 嚻, bersuara seperti burung magpie, dan memakannya menyembuhkan sakit perut serta menghentikan 衕.
claims.quote: 有鳥焉，其狀如夸父，四翼、一目、犬尾，名曰嚻，其音如鵲，食之已腹痛，可以止衕。

claims.statement: Chisongzi is an immortal in Chinese legend, also written with the alternative characters 赤诵子.
claims.statement_id: Chisongzi adalah tokoh abadi dalam legenda Tiongkok, juga disebut Chisongzi dengan varian penulisan 赤诵子.
claims.quote: 赤松子又名赤诵子，号左圣南极南岳真人，又稱左仙太虚真人，秦汉传说中的上古仙人，與王子喬並列為長生的代表。

claims.statement: The Taiping Huanyu Ji associates his ascent to heaven with Mount Chisong in Jinhua.
claims.statement_id: Taiping Huanyu Ji mengaitkan kenaikannya ke langit dengan Gunung Chisong di Jinhua.
claims.quote: 《太平寰宇记》说赤松子是在金华的赤松山（金华山），以火自焚尸解升天，其处为赤松涧，故山上有赤松祠。

claims.statement: The Liexian Zhuan places Chisongzi as a rain master in Shennong's time.
claims.statement_id: Liexian Zhuan menempatkan Chisongzi sebagai ahli hujan pada masa Shennong.
claims.quote: 刘向的《列仙传》记载赤松子本是神农时人，为雨师，他服食水玉，把它教给神农，能够在烈火中任火烧烤。赤松子常常去昆仑山上，在西王母的石室之中歇息，随风雨自由上下。炎帝的小女儿曾跟随他，亦成仙飞升而去。又据《韩诗外传》载，赤松子曾为帝喾之师。

claims.statement: He is depicted as enduring fire and moving with rain and wind.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan tahan terhadap api dan dapat mengikuti hujan serta angin.
claims.quote: 刘向的《列仙传》记载赤松子本是神农时人，为雨师，他服食水玉，把它教给神农，能够在烈火中任火烧烤。赤松子常常去昆仑山上，在西王母的石室之中歇息，随风雨自由上下。炎帝的小女儿曾跟随他，亦成仙飞升而去。又据《韩诗外传》载，赤松子曾为帝喾之师。

claims.statement: In the account he often visits Kunlun, staying in Xi Wangmu's stone chamber.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah itu ia kerap berada di Kunlun, dalam ruang batu milik Xi Wangmu.
claims.quote: 刘向的《列仙传》记载赤松子本是神农时人，为雨师，他服食水玉，把它教给神农，能够在烈火中任火烧烤。赤松子常常去昆仑山上，在西王母的石室之中歇息，随风雨自由上下。炎帝的小女儿曾跟随他，亦成仙飞升而去。又据《韩诗外传》载，赤松子曾为帝喾之师。

claims.statement: Sources give differing accounts of the substance he consumes for immortality.
claims.statement_id: Sumber-sumber memberikan keterangan berbeda tentang bahan yang dimakannya untuk menjadi abadi.
claims.quote: 关于赤松子服水玉一事，文献中记载中多有不同。《山海经·南山经》注中说赤松子所服食的水玉就是水精（水晶），干宝的《搜神记》则称为冰玉散，葛洪的《抱朴子》则说赤松子服食的是神丹，并有赤松子丹法传世。相传也是葛洪所著的《神仙传》中则称黃初平（皇初平）为赤松子，服松腊茯苓。《丹台录》则称赤松子为昆林仙伯，辖牿南岳山，可化玉为水而服。

claims.statement: In the text 《列仙傳》, 赤松子 is the rain master (雨師) of Shennong's time; he took 水玉 and taught it to Shennong, could enter fire and burn himself, often went to Mount Kunlun, stayed in Xi Wangmu's stone chamber, and went up and down with wind and rain.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks 《列仙傳》, 赤松子 adalah ahli hujan (雨師) pada zaman Shennong; ia makan 水玉 dan mengajarkannya kepada Shennong, mampu masuk api dan membakar dirinya, sering ke Gunung Kunlun, tinggal di ruang batu Xi Wangmu, dan naik turun mengikuti angin dan hujan.
claims.quote: 赤松子者，神農時雨師也。服水玉以教神農，能入火自燒。往往至崑崙山上，常止西王母石室中，隨風雨上下。

claims.statement: The text adds that the youngest daughter of Emperor Yan (炎帝) followed him, also became an immortal, and they left together; in the time of Gaoxin (高辛) he again served as rain master, and the rain master of later times derives from him.
claims.statement_id: Teks itu menambahkan bahwa putri bungsu Kaisar Yan (炎帝) mengikutinya, juga menjadi abadi, dan mereka pergi bersama; pada masa Gaoxin (高辛) ia kembali menjadi ahli hujan, dan ahli hujan zaman itu bersumber darinya.
claims.quote: 炎帝少女追之，亦得仙，俱去。至高辛時，復為雨師。今之雨師本是焉。

claims.statement: The eulogy verse in the text pictures 赤松子 and the girl flying hand in hand, leaping onto the long wind toward the 玄圃, and setting the pattern for governing rain.
claims.statement_id: Bait pujian dalam teks itu menggambarkan 赤松子 dan sang gadis terbang bergandengan tangan, melompat ke angin panjang menuju 玄圃, dan menjadi teladan yang mengatur hujan.
claims.quote: 眇眇赤松，飄飄少女。接手翻飛，泠然雙舉。縱身長風，俄翼玄圃。妙達巽坎，作範司雨。

claims.statement: Hairen are sea dwelling humans or humanoids in Chinese lore, called kaijin in Japanese sources.
claims.statement_id: Hairen adalah manusia atau makhluk menyerupai manusia penghuni laut dalam khazanah Tiongkok, disebut kaijin dalam sumber Jepang.
claims.quote: A hairen (海人, "sea-human") is a sea-dwelling human or humanoid in Chinese lore, also called  kaijin (海人) by Japanese sources.

claims.statement: Chinese language accounts written by Europeans describe webbed hands and feet.
claims.statement_id: Catatan berbahasa Tionghoa yang ditulis orang Eropa menggambarkan tangan dan kaki berselaput.
claims.quote: According to a Chinese texts which were actually authored by Europeans, the hairen was human-like overall but possessed webbed feet and hands, and one was captured in Holland, who had loose drooping skin on her whole body, almost like she wore a piece of garment (specifically a paofu or long robe).

claims.statement: Edo accounts such as Yamato Honzō repeat the description of a creature with skin hanging like hakama trousers.
claims.statement_id: Catatan Edo seperti Yamato Honzō mengulang kisah makhluk dengan kulit menjuntai seperti celana hakama.
claims.quote: The account of the "sea-humans" also recurred in Japanese sources dating to the Edo Period, such as Kaibara Ekken's Yamato honzō, which describe the creature as having skin that hangs down to the ground, like a pair of hakama trousers being worn.

claims.statement: Giulio Aleni and Ferdinand Verbiest publish descriptions of hairen in Chinese language works.
claims.statement_id: Giulio Aleni dan Ferdinand Verbiest menerbitkan keterangan hairen dalam karya berbahasa Tionghoa.
claims.quote: Books written by Europeans and published in the Chinese language during the Ming and Qing dynasties mention the hairen. Italian Jesuit Giulio Aleni (Chinese name: Airulüe 艾儒略) wrote in his Zhifang waiji (simplified Chinese: 职方外纪; traditional Chinese: 職方外紀, "Records of Regions beyond the Jurisdiction of the Imperial Geographer", 1623) that there are two types of hairen.

claims.statement: One story describes a creature captured and presented to a king, then released because it could not be tamed.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu kisah menyebut makhluk yang ditangkap dan diberikan kepada raja, lalu dilepas karena tidak dapat dijinakkan.
claims.quote: The first type was overall human-like, with both beards and eyebrows, but having hands and feet which were webbed, like those of wild ducks. An individual was captured in the Western (European) sea, and presented to a certain king, but ate nothing, and having failed to tame it, the king was forced to release it back to sea, and the liberated creature clapped its hands and laughed loudly.

claims.statement: The scholarship summarised in the article connects the female hairen with the reported capture in Holland in 1403.
claims.statement_id: Kajian yang diringkas artikel menghubungkan perempuan hairen dengan kisah penangkapan di Belanda pada 1403.
claims.quote: This female hairen has been determined to be the one captured in Holland in 1403

claims.statement: In the 海和尚 section of the 《海語》, which describes a human-headed, turtle-bodied creature that climbs onto a ship's prow, an annotation quotes the 《草木子》 on the 海人: Shao Zi (邵子) holds that every land creature must have a counterpart in water, and sea merchants say a 海人 appears shaped like a monk, rather small, boards the boat and sits; the crew must stay silent until it dives back, otherwise a great wind will capsize the boat.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bagian 海和尚 pada 《海語》, yang menggambarkan makhluk berkepala manusia dan bertubuh kura-kura yang naik ke haluan kapal, sebuah catatan mengutip 《草木子》 tentang 海人: Shao Zi (邵子) berpendapat makhluk darat pasti punya padanan di air, dan menurut pedagang laut 海人 muncul berbentuk seperti biksu, agak kecil, naik ke perahu dan duduk; awak harus diam sampai ia menyelam kembali, kalau tidak angin besar akan membalikkan perahu.
claims.quote: 物怪 海和尚 海和尚人首鼈身足差長而無甲舟行遇者率虞不利𢎞治初吾廣督學大僉淮陽韋彦質先生將視學瓊州陸至徐聞方登海舟此物升鷁首而蹲舉舟皆泣謂有魚腹之憂議將禳之先生方嚴人不敢白也詰旦抵瓊留十許日試士都畢泛海而還若履平地後遷福建憲都考終于家語曰妖不勝徳〈草木子邵子曰陸生之物水中必具計必有海人嘗聞之海賈云有海人出形如僧人頗小登舟而坐至則戒舟人寂然不動少頃復沉水否則大風翻舟

claims.statement: Hua Po is a tree spirit in Chinese lore.
claims.statement_id: Hua Po adalah roh pohon dalam cerita Tiongkok.
claims.quote: 花魄（かはく　Hua-po）は、中国に伝わる木の精の一種。3人以上が首吊り自殺した木に、自殺者達の生前の無念が凝り固まって誕生すると言われる。

claims.statement: Its formation is linked to the regrets of the dead after at least three people hang themselves from the tree.
claims.statement_id: Kelahirannya dikaitkan dengan penyesalan orang yang meninggal setelah setidaknya tiga orang menggantung diri pada pohon itu.
claims.quote: 花魄（かはく　Hua-po）は、中国に伝わる木の精の一種。3人以上が首吊り自殺した木に、自殺者達の生前の無念が凝り固まって誕生すると言われる。

claims.statement: The spirit is described as a pale beautiful woman the size of a palm.
claims.statement_id: Roh ini digambarkan sebagai perempuan cantik berkulit putih seukuran telapak tangan.
claims.quote:
掌サイズの大きさで、肌の白い美女の姿をしている。
その鳴き声はインコに似ているとされる。
そのまま放っておくと干からびるが、水をかけると元通りになると言う。

claims.statement: Its voice resembles a parakeet.
claims.statement_id: Suaranya menyerupai parkit.
claims.quote:
掌サイズの大きさで、肌の白い美女の姿をしている。
その鳴き声はインコに似ているとされる。
そのまま放っておくと干からびるが、水をかけると元通りになると言う。

claims.statement: It is said to dry out if left alone and recover when sprinkled with water.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikatakan mengering jika dibiarkan, lalu pulih ketika diperciki air.
claims.quote:
掌サイズの大きさで、肌の白い美女の姿をしている。
その鳴き声はインコに似ているとされる。
そのまま放っておくと干からびるが、水をかけると元通りになると言う。

claims.statement: In the story "Huapo" in 《子不語》 (Zibuyu), a scholar surnamed Xie who was studying on Zhanggong Mountain heard a chirping in the trees like a parrot. On going closer he saw a beautiful woman about five cun tall, hairless, white all over like jade, with a look of grief about her eyes and brows.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah 〈花魄〉 pada 《子不語》 (Zibuyu), seorang terpelajar bermarga Xie yang belajar di Gunung Zhanggong mendengar bunyi berkicau di hutan pohon yang mirip beo. Saat mendekat, ia melihat seorang perempuan cantik setinggi sekitar lima cun, tanpa bulu di tubuhnya, putih mengilap seperti giok, dengan raut sedih di antara kedua matanya.
claims.quote: 婺源士人謝某，讀書張公山。早起，聞樹林鳥聲啁啾，有似鸚哥。因近視之，乃一美女，長五寸許，赤身無毛，通體潔白如玉，眉目間有愁苦之狀。

claims.statement: The scholar took her home, kept her in a cage and fed her rice. She chattered to people but could not be understood. After some days, exposed to the sun, she dried up and died.
claims.statement_id: Sang terpelajar membawanya pulang dan menyimpannya dalam sangkar serta memberinya nasi. Makhluk itu berbicara terus-menerus kepada orang tetapi ucapannya tidak dapat dimengerti. Setelah beberapa hari terkena sinar matahari, ia mengering dan mati.
claims.quote: 遂攜以歸，女無懼色。乃畜籠中，以飯喂之。向人絮語，了不可辨。畜數日，為太陽所照，竟成枯臘而死。

claims.statement: A xiaolian (孝廉) named Hong said the creature was called 花魄 (Huapo), formed from the aggrieved and anguished qi of a tree on which people had hanged themselves three times, and that pouring water on it could still revive it; when tried, it proved so.
claims.statement_id: Seorang bergelar xiaolian (孝廉) bermarga Hong berkata bahwa makhluk itu bernama 花魄 (Huapo), terbentuk dari hawa dendam dan derita pada pohon tempat orang gantung diri sampai tiga kali, dan bahwa menyiramnya dengan air masih dapat menghidupkannya; ketika dicoba, memang demikian.
claims.quote: 洪孝廉字麟聞之曰：「此名花魄，凡樹經三次人縊死者，其冤苦之氣結成此物，沃以水，猶可活也。」試之果然。

claims.statement: Villagers crowded round to look. Fearing the stir, Xie put her back in the tree, and shortly afterwards a large strange bird seized her in its beak and flew off.
claims.statement_id: Penduduk desa berbondong-bondong datang menonton. Karena khawatir menimbulkan kehebohan, Xie meletakkannya kembali di pohon, dan tak lama kemudian seekor burung besar yang aneh menyambarnya dan terbang membawanya.
claims.quote: 里人聚觀者，如雲而至。謝恐招搖，乃仍送之樹上。須臾間，一大怪鳥銜之飛去。

claims.statement: Kaimingshou is a divine creature in the Hai Nei Xi Jing section of the Shan Hai Jing.
claims.statement_id: Kaimingshou adalah makhluk ilahi dalam bagian Hai Nei Xi Jing pada Shan Hai Jing.
claims.quote: 開明獣（かいめいじゅう）は、 古代中国の地理書『山海経』の「海内西経」に記述のある神獣。

claims.statement: It guards the nine gates of Kunlun, the heavenly ruler's dwelling in the lower world.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjaga sembilan gerbang Kunlun, kediaman penguasa langit di dunia bawah.
claims.quote: 天帝の下界の都である崑崙の丘にある九つの門を守っている。その姿は大きな体で虎に似て、九つある首は全て人間の顔だという。

claims.statement: Its body is large and tigerlike.
claims.statement_id: Tubuhnya besar dan menyerupai harimau.
claims.quote: 天帝の下界の都である崑崙の丘にある九つの門を守っている。その姿は大きな体で虎に似て、九つある首は全て人間の顔だという。

claims.statement: Its nine heads each have a human face.
claims.statement_id: Kesembilan kepalanya mempunyai wajah manusia.
claims.quote: 天帝の下界の都である崑崙の丘にある九つの門を守っている。その姿は大きな体で虎に似て、九つある首は全て人間の顔だという。

claims.statement: The description of a single principal eastern gate is identified as absent from the Shan Hai Jing.
claims.statement_id: Uraian tentang satu gerbang utama timur disebut tidak terdapat dalam Shan Hai Jing.
claims.quote: 「崑崙山の宮殿で、9ある門の内、東側の正門である『開明門』の門番をしている」等と紹介している書籍も存在するが、山海経にそのような記述はない。

claims.statement: Kaimingshou is sometimes identified with Lu Wu because of their similar characteristics.
claims.statement_id: Kaimingshou kadang disamakan dengan Lu Wu karena kemiripan sifatnya.
claims.quote: 性質が開明獣と似通っていることから、両者は同一視されることがある。 脚注

claims.statement: The Overseas-West-within section of the Shanhaijing calls the 昆侖之虛 the lower capital of the Emperor (帝之下都), with nine gates each guarded by the 開明獸, where the hundred spirits dwell.
claims.statement_id: Shanhaijing bagian Haineixi Jing menyebut 昆侖之虛 sebagai kota bawah milik Kaisar (帝之下都) dengan sembilan gerbang yang masing-masing dijaga 開明獸, tempat berkumpul seratus dewa.
claims.quote: 海內昆侖之虛，在西北，帝之下都。昆侖之虛，方八百里，高萬仞。上有木禾，長五尋，大五圍。面有九井，以玉為檻。面有九門，門有開明獸守之，百神之所在。

claims.statement: The same text says the 開明獸 has a large tiger-like body and nine heads, all with human faces, and stands on Kunlun facing east.
claims.statement_id: Teks yang sama menyebut 開明獸 bertubuh besar mirip harimau dengan sembilan kepala yang semuanya berwajah manusia, berdiri di atas Kunlun menghadap ke timur.
claims.quote: 昆侖南淵深三百仞。開明獸身大類虎而九首，皆人面，東嚮立昆侖上。

issues.message: Mengusulkan tradisi baru: "Cerita kriptid Xinjiang".

claims.statement: The Kanas Lake Monster is a creature reportedly living in Kanas Lake, Xinjiang; its existence remains unconfirmed.
claims.statement_id: Monster Danau Kanas adalah makhluk yang dilaporkan hidup di Danau Kanas, Xinjiang; keberadaannya belum dipastikan.
claims.quote: 喀纳斯湖水怪（英语：Kanas Lake Monster），是据传生活在中国新疆维吾尔自治区喀纳斯湖中的不明生物。与世界各地的其它湖怪不同，喀纳斯湖水怪并非传说的爬虫类或哺乳类，而类似于鱼类的生物。

claims.statement: The CERNET report presents giant taimen as a proposed explanation for the monster.
claims.statement_id: Laporan CERNET menyebut taimen raksasa sebagai penjelasan yang diajukan untuk monster itu.
claims.quote: The "lake monster" is thought to be giant taimen.

claims.statement: The report states that the sighted objects require further investigation before being identified as lake monsters.
claims.statement_id: Laporan itu menyatakan bahwa objek penampakan masih membutuhkan penyelidikan untuk disebut monster danau.
claims.quote: Whether the two objects are legendary "lake monsters" requires further investigation.

claims.statement: China Today also lists a giant red fish, the Siberian taimen, among the hypotheses discussed.
claims.statement_id: China Today juga mencantumkan ikan merah raksasa Siberian taimen di antara hipotesis yang dibahas.
claims.quote: first, it is a giant red fish, called Siberian taimen.

claims.statement: China Today notes that since some claimed to have discovered and photographed a "giant lake monster" in Kanas Lake in 1980, the Kanas Lake monster has remained a well-known, unsolved "mystery".
claims.statement_id: China Today mencatat bahwa sejak sebagian orang mengaku menemukan dan memotret "monster danau raksasa" di Danau Kanas pada 1980, monster Danau Kanas tetap menjadi "misteri" terkenal yang belum terpecahkan.
claims.quote: Since some claimed that they had discovered and photographed a “giant lake monster” in the Kanas Lake in 1980, Kanas Lake monster has remained a well-known, unsolved “mystery.”

claims.statement: The CERNET report mentions bulls, horses and sheep that disappeared along the lake and asks whether they were really swallowed up by the "monsters".
claims.statement_id: Laporan CERNET menyinggung sapi, kuda, dan domba yang hilang di sekitar danau dan mempertanyakan apakah hewan-hewan itu benar-benar ditelan "monster" tersebut.
claims.quote: For those bulls, horses and sheep disappeared along the lake, were they really swallowed up by the "monsters"?

claims.statement: Klu are dragon deities or water spirits in Tibetan tradition.

claims.quote: 鲁（藏語：ཀླུ，威利转写：klu，THL：lü），或半音半意译云鲁龙，是藏族文化中的龙神。在苯教传说中，鲁龙居住在五個方向的山林池澤中，其中有善類，帶來豐收和幸福，也有惡類，帶來疾疫和災難；魯龙是重要的水界神靈，传说作为天神之子的吐蕃王赞普，最初皆与龙女或神女婚配；佛教傳入藏地後，魯龙和印度文化中的那伽神龍（蛇龍類神獸）等同起來。考古認為魯龙文化的起源非常久遠，可能是漢藏民族的共同信仰，在纳西、彝、傈僳等其他民族中都有流传，和汉地的龙文化也可能同源。

claims.statement: Early Klu forms are variable and can include different aquatic animals.

claims.quote: 根據對遺跡、壁畫和史料記載等的考古研究，推断“魯”龍神崇拜起源於吐蕃以前的原始社會。早期的鲁龙形象复杂多变，可以附身或化身爲水生動物，沒有固定的形象，甚至可以泛指魚、蝦、蛙、蛇、蝎、蟹等。牠們能帶來420多種疾病，如瘟疫、梅毒、傷寒、天花、麻風等，藏人稱之為“龍病”。在近代的川西南藏区仍流传着“亵渎了水中的神灵，身上就会起水泡、长脓疮”的说法，是“龙病”观点的遗留。

claims.quote: 在苯教经过辛饶米沃祖师的改革而进入恰苯时期後，鲁龙被作为重要的神祇加以供奉，其形象演變為多種動物的綜合。苯教《大品黑白花濟龍經》（《十万龙经》）記載，龍神有人身、馬頭，或蛇頭、虎頭、熊頭、鼠頭、羊頭、牛頭、豹頭、豕頭、鹿頭、狼頭、孔雀頭等等不同形象，且都有蛇尾或魚尾。這與漢地龍形象的演變頗有相近之處，即“九擬”理論——角似鹿（最初漢地龍沒有角）、頭似駝、眼似兔、項似蛇、腹似蜃、鱗似魚、爪似鷹、掌似虎、身如牛。此時期，魯龍的故事也在原始傳說基礎上豐富而具體起來。如苯教经典《花黑白十万龙经》（简称《十万龙经》，也稱《十二萬龍經》）中寫道，魯龍是世界誕生之母，故稱“龍母”，它們居住在水域中，或山林中，也說住在海底龍宮，守护着无数财宝。藏学家海爾姆特·霍夫曼在《西藏的宗教》一书中写道：“这些龙的最初的住所是河和湖，甚至是些井；他们在水底有家，守卫着秘密的财富。

claims.quote: 普雷斯帕湖怪物（英文：Prespa Lake Monster）是指出没于欧洲巴尔干半岛普雷斯帕湖的湖怪。普雷斯帕湖怪物在当地一直有所传闻，其被描述为类似长颈尼斯湖怪的动物。2012年，一对夫妇在阿尔巴尼亚尼维察（Nivica）附近希腊湖区目击湖怪出没。英国广播公司对普雷斯帕湖展开调查，但没有收获。2017年，阿尔巴尼亚普雷托村（Pretor）再度有目击者发现长颈湖怪，并拍下一段视频。之后退休地理学教授Sima Jonoski与记者们一同展开调查，但没有发现湖怪踪迹。有理论认为普雷斯帕湖怪物其实是湖中的鲶鱼，但反对者认为鲶鱼与影像中的湖怪形象不符。神秘动物学研究者安德鲁·麦格拉思（Andrew McGrath）对2017年12月流出的湖怪影像真实性表示怀疑，认为这可能是一场骗局。

claims.quote: A ro-langs (Tibetan: རོ་ལང) is a zombie-like creature from Tibetan folklore. claims.statement: Si is a single horned oxlike animal in ancient Chinese texts; its zoological identification requires care.
claims.statement_id: Si adalah hewan bertanduk satu yang menyerupai sapi dalam teks kuno Tiongkok; identifikasi zoologisnya memerlukan kehati-hatian.
claims.quote: 兕（呉音: じ、漢音: し、拼音: sì）は、古代中国の文献に出てくる動物の一種。牛に似た一本角の獣。

claims.statement: Texts such as the Analects and Zhuangzi mention Si as a fierce beast alongside tigers and jiao.
claims.statement_id: Teks seperti Analects dan Zhuangzi menyebut Si sebagai contoh hewan buas bersama harimau dan jiao.
claims.quote: 『論語』や『荘子』といった先秦の様々な文献で、「虎」や「蛟」（蛟竜）と並ぶ猛獣の代名詞として言及される。

claims.statement: Guo Pu's Erya commentary describes it as single horned and dark blue.
claims.statement_id: Komentar Guo Pu pada Erya menggambarkannya bertanduk satu dan berwarna biru gelap.
claims.quote: 『爾雅』郭璞注などによれば、一本角で、色は青（青黒）、重さは千斤だった。

claims.statement: The Erya compares Si with an ox and xi with a pig.
claims.statement_id: Erya membandingkan Si dengan sapi dan xi dengan babi.
claims.quote: 『山海経』によれば、兕は「犀」などと一緒に中国内外各地に生息していた。『爾雅』本文によれば、兕が牛に似ているのに対し、犀は豚に似ていた。

claims.statement: Several texts associate Si with the hunts of Chu rulers.
claims.statement_id: Sejumlah teks menghubungkan Si dengan perburuan penguasa Chu.
claims.quote: 兕は楚国と縁が深い。『古本竹書紀年』によれば、周の昭王が楚に南征に訪れた際、大兕に遭遇したという。また様々な文献において、楚の君主が雲夢の地で御狩する猛獣として登場する（例:『公孫龍子』跡府篇などに伝わる「楚弓楚得」説話、『戦国策』楚策一、『楚辞』招魂）。

claims.statement: The Zhou Li and other texts mention Si hides as material for armour.
claims.statement_id: Zhou Li dan teks lain menyebut kulit Si sebagai bahan untuk baju zirah.
claims.quote: 『周礼』考工記などによれば、兕や犀の皮革は甲冑の材料として利用されていた。『荀子』議兵篇などによれば、そのような用法は楚人の慣習だった。

claims.quote: 鹿王，是台灣鄒族傳說中的神鹿，不僅有強大的能力，還可以變換身體的外貌。

claims.statement: Its initially ordinary deer form can grow enormously large.

claims.quote: 鹿王的外表跟一般的鹿差不多，但牠的身形可以變得相當巨大，還有變成人或巨人、甚至詛咒他人的能力。

claims.statement: In a story of two hunting brothers, the elder avoids a deer that grows larger when aimed at.

claims.quote: 傳說中以前有對兄弟長期輪流去宿瓦納（Nsoana，位於今嘉義縣阿里山鄉）的山上獵鹿，鹿群中有頭鹿只要被武器瞄準就會越變越大，哥哥知道那頭鹿不可隨意射殺，所以都會改獵別隻，並且告訴弟弟，但不服輸的弟弟在一次打獵中發現那頭鹿，並將牠射殺，又因為太緊張了，直接丟下鹿王跑回家，後來他折返回去查看時（他有請哥哥跟他一起去，但半路上哥哥就跑回家了），沒有找到鹿，但草叢中卻出現一個眼睛如日月般明亮的男巨人，男巨人怒吼著抓住弟弟，用力甩了幾下後把他摔向旁邊的樹幹，弟弟就此斃命。

claims.statement: The younger brother kills the deer, then returns and encounters a male giant who kills him.
claims.statement_id: Adiknya membunuh rusa itu, lalu kembali dan menemukan raksasa lelaki yang membunuhnya.
claims.quote: 後來他折返回去查看時（他有請哥哥跟他一起去，但半路上哥哥就跑回家了），沒有找到鹿，但草叢中卻出現一個眼睛如日月般明亮的男巨人，男巨人怒吼著抓住弟弟，用力甩了幾下後把他摔向旁邊的樹幹，弟弟就此斃命。

claims.statement: Another version describes a deer hide flying to strangle a hunter after a warning about its gall bladder is violated.
claims.statement_id: Versi lain mengisahkan kulit rusa yang terbang mencekik pemburu setelah larangan mengenai empedunya dilanggar.
claims.quote: 除了以上傳說外，也有鹿變成人負傷而逃，並且趁機把追上來的獵人的頭抓去撞樹幹來殺死他、或是鹿在死前告訴獵人不要刺破牠的膽，但獵人還是刺破了，導致剝下來的鹿皮飛去勒死了獵人的版本。
